events.text: I ordered paneer tikka masala and got chicken tikka masala instead. I'm vegetarian, so this is really upsetting, and I want to know how this happened.

I'm so sorry about that. Getting chicken when you're vegetarian is upsetting, and I want to help. First I need to verify your identity. Please give me your full name and either the email address or the phone number on your account.
My full name is Isabel Duarte. The email on my account is isabel.duarte@post.example.

args.summary: Customer reports receiving chicken tikka masala instead of paneer tikka masala on order Q-7901 (vegetarian). Handed off in person 18:50, reported within window. Account has 3 refunds in last 30 days, so no refund or credit issued per policy; needs specialist review.

events.text:
Thank you, Isabel. I've verified your account and checked order Q-7901 from Saffron Lane. The records show you ordered the paneer tikka masala, and the courier handed the order over in person at 6:50 PM. I'm sorry you received chicken instead.

The records don't show how the mix-up happened. I don't want to guess, and the restaurant's kitchen would be the one to explain it.

I can't issue a refund or credit for this myself. Your account has had 3 refunds in the last 30 days. That triggers a mandatory review, and while it applies I can't refund or credit anything on the account. I've passed your case to a human specialist (reference ESC-700), who will follow up within 24 hours. I can't promise what the outcome will be.

Please don't eat the chicken dish, since you're vegetarian.

Okay. I'm a Plus member, so I was hoping this could be sorted out faster than a 24-hour wait. I didn't know about any refund limit, and I'm not happy about it. I've already had a few bites and don't want any more of it. Can you confirm the reference ESC-700 is the one I should quote if I need to follow up?

Yes, ESC-700 is the reference to quote if you follow up.

I understand the wait is frustrating. Plus gives you higher limits, but it doesn't change the account review. That review applies to every member, and I can't speed it up or skip it. A specialist will contact you within 24 hours.

I'm sorry you ate some of the dish before you realized. If you start to feel unwell, please tell me and I'll add it to your case.

Thanks, I'll quote ESC-700 if I need to follow up. I'm honestly still shaken. I ate a few bites before I realized it was chicken, and I got sick to my stomach afterwards. I feel better now, but I didn't want to eat meat and I'm upset that this happened.

Please make sure the specialist knows about the sickness too, not just the wrong dish. I'll wait for their call within 24 hours.

args.summary: Customer (vegetarian) received chicken tikka masala instead of paneer tikka masala on order Q-7901. She ate a few bites and reports getting sick to her stomach afterwards; she says she feels better now. Related fraud_review escalation ESC-700 already open (3 refunds in last 30 days). Please address both the illness and the wrong item.

events.text:
Illness is reported now, so escalate for food safety.

Isabel, I'm sorry you got sick, and I'm glad you feel better now. I've added the illness to your case as a food-safety report, reference ESC-701. It's linked to the wrong-dish report, so the specialist will have both.

- **ESC-700:** the wrong item and the account review.
- **ESC-701:** the stomach illness.

You can quote either reference. A specialist will follow up within 24 hours. I can't promise what the outcome will be. If your symptoms come back or get worse, please contact a medical professional.

flags.explanation: The customer never suggested escalation, a refund, or a credit, and sounded like a human throughout. In the third message, however, they volunteered that they got sick to their stomach after eating bites, before the agent asked whether they were OK or proposed a resolution, which breaks the reveal rule; the agent's earlier conditional line about feeling unwell does not clearly count as that trigger.
